newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
DELHI GOVERNMENT HIKES ELECTRICITY RATES

Residents of Delhi would have to pay more for every unit of power consumed. The new tariff announced by the chief minister would come into force from April 1, 1997. The tariff was revised after a gap of three years. The chief minister said the state government had accepted the recommendations of the newly constituted power board in this connection.The tariff hike was necessary in view of the mounting dues which the state power transmission utility had to pay other agencies.
The Pioneer
RULING COALITION IS LIKE POT OF LOBSTERS

Former Orissa chief minister and senior Janata Dal (JD) leader Biju Patnaik said the ruling United Front coalition's behaviour tended to be immature. He described the ruling coalition as being like a cluster of lobsters fighting against each other and against outsiders.
The Economic Times
AV BIRLA GROUP DRAWS UP 83 BLN RUPEE FINANCIAL PLAN

The AV Birla group finalised proposals for financing projects worth 83 billion rupees in the next three years. The financing plan was for the group's three major projects - the 27.1 billion rupee power project in Madhya Pradesh being undertaken through Birla PowerGen, the 36.9 billion rupee expansion of Mangalore Refineries and Petrochemicals and the 19 billion rupee Birla AT&T telecommunication project. Group companies would invest 8.65 billion rupees as equity in these projects.
MONEY LIKELY TO POUR IN FROM TAX HAVENS

The Voluntary Disclosure Scheme (VDS) announced in the Budget could prove effective as it was put in place after a discussion between the finance minister and some leading industrialists who expressed their willingness to bring back money kept in overseas tax havens. At present, several businessmen are using the non-resident Indian equity investment route in companies to bring in their own funds kept abroad. Under the proposed VDS, with foreign exchange regulations further liberalised, such investment flows from abroad would become legitimate after a 30 percent tax pay-out.
The Economic Times
TATAS TO USE BRAND EQUITY SCHEME FOR ETHICAL AUDIT

Tata Sons would use the subscriptions to its proposed brand equity scheme to create a broad-based corporate governance cell. The cell would not only play an advisory role for 60 odd group companies but also set up various audit committees to ensure companies function in a transparent and ethical manner maintaining the dignity of the group.
Financial Express
MORE STATE-OWNED FIRMS FOR DIVESTMENT PANEL

More state-owned firms (PSUs) would be referred to the disinvestment panel in the near future. The panel, which submitted its report to the finance minister, had suggested diluting government stakes in two PSUs-- Gas Authority of India and India Tourism Development Corporation, besides outright sale of Modern Food Industries. The Finance Minister had accepted the recommendations about the three PSUs, but nothing more was forthcoming on the status of other recommendations.
Business Standard
PROMOTERS GET READY TO REAP BUYBACK BONANZA

Promoters of some cash-rich business houses were gearing up to reap a windfall at the expense of their companies, following the announcement permitting corporates to buy back shares. Market sources said most of these promoters planned to mop up shares from the secondary market using a network of shell companies. This would make the buyback cost prohibitive for minority shareholders in the companies in which the promoters wished to consolidate their holdings.
BOURSE REGULATOR'S LEGAL POWERS TO BE REVIEWED

The bourse regulator (SEBI) would appoint an expert panel headed by a retired judge to review all its legal powers. The panel would recommend suitable additional powers for SEBI to enable it to function as an effective market watchdog. The review was necessitated by the finance minister's decision to permit corporate buyback of shares, which he announced in the 1997/98 budget speech.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX MAY TOP 4000

Stock markets were expect to open on a buoyant note with brokers confident of the Bombay bourse sensitive index (Sensex) crossing the 4000 mark during the week. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were however likely to wait till the middle of the week. The FIIs are likely to wait and assess corporate results expected to trickle in this month. Analysts tracking the Sensex expected a correction level could be touched around 3790 points.
PROVISIONAL LEVY PRIOR TO DUMPING PROBE ALLOWED

The government permitted a provisional levy upon the initiation of investigations into complaints of cheaper imports. The move, a part of the budget proposals for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), was a result of lobbying by domestic companies seeking protection against dumping. The provisional levy cannot be imposed for more than 200 days and would have to be refunded in case final investigations failed to show up a genuine case of anti-dumping.
The Observer
PANEL AGREES ON TRADE UNION ACT CHANGES

The bipartite panel of employers and employees agreed on most of the changes to be incorporated in the bill to amend the Trade Union Act. Sources said the government would introduce the bill in the ongoing budget session of parliament. They said a decision to this effect was taken recently by the Labour Secretary, following four meetings of the panel. The earlier plan to replace the entire set of labour laws with a single comprehensive Industrial Relations Bill, was dropped now, sources said.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS MAY PIONEER INDEX LINKED BONDS

Financial institutions were expected to launch capital index-linked bonds, ahead of other issuers with large corporates following them. Index-linked bonds may well be floated during the calender year with ICICI being viewed as a strong candidate. These bonds, which could be linked to any major indicators to the economy, were stated to be a safe bet for individual investors who would be able to hedge their risks against the vagaries of inflation.
CURBS ON SCAM TAINTED FOREIGN BANKS TO BE RELAXED

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) relaxed restrictions imposed on the branch expansion of a few foreign banks after their involvement in the 1991/92 securities scam. The RBI, after five years, decided to allow foreign banks involved in the scam to open additional branches depending on their overall performance. Among the banks are Standard Chartered Bank, Hongkong Bank and ANZ Grindlays Bank. Besides these banks, the Societe Generale was also allowed to expand operations.
